name: Whatnot
tagline: Whatnot seller fee calculator: 8% commission (less with volume) plus 2.9% + $0.30 processing, and payout.
fee_summary: Whatnot charges an 8% commission on the item sale price for most categories (4% for coins), falling as low as 3.5%–6.5% once your 28-day sales pass $15,000, plus a 2.9% + $0.30 payment processing fee on the full order total including buyer-paid shipping and tax.

sources.title: Whatnot Help Center – Whatnot Seller Fees and Commissions Schedule

inputs.label: Shipping the buyer pays
inputs.help: Shipping charged to the buyer on this order. Processing is charged on it; commission is not.

inputs.label: What the item cost you
inputs.help: Purchase or sourcing cost of the item.

inputs.label: What the label costs you
inputs.help: Your shipping label and packaging cost for this order.

worked_example.explanation: A sports card sells in a live show for $50 and the buyer pays $6 shipping. At the standard tier, commission is 8% of the $50 item price = $4.00. Payment processing is 2.9% of the $56 order total = $1.62 plus $0.30 = $1.92. Fees total $5.92, so the payout is $56.00 − $5.92 = $50.08. After the $20 card cost and the $6 label, profit is $24.08.

content.intro:
Whatnot is a live-shopping marketplace where sellers run auctions and buy-it-now sales on video, plus a standard marketplace for fixed-price listings. Sports cards, trading card games, coins, collectibles, and fashion are the biggest categories, and sellers range from hobbyists streaming on weekends to full-time card shops.

Since September 21, 2026, Whatnot's commission depends on your category and your total sales over the previous 28 days. The standard rate, for anyone under $15,000 in that window, is 8% of the item sale price in every category except coins, which is 4%. Above $15,000 the rate steps down through six tiers: sports and TCG bottom out at 6.5% past $500,000, fashion at 4.5%, other collectibles at 5%, coins at 3.5%, and everything else at 4%. Your rate is locked for each four-week period, and cancelled orders are subtracted from your total.

Every order also pays a 2.9% + $0.30 payment processing fee, charged on the full amount the buyer pays, including shipping and sales tax. Commission itself is charged on the item price only.

For a $50 card with $6 buyer-paid shipping at the standard tier, that works out to $4.00 commission and $1.92 processing, leaving $50.08 before your label and product cost.
how_fees_work: Commission, standard tier (under $15,000 in sales over the 28-day period): 8% of the item sale price in sports, TCG, fashion, other collectibles, and all other categories; 4% for coins and money.

Volume tiers: your combined sales across all categories, live shows and marketplace, over a four-week (28-day) period set your tier for the next period. Tier 1 starts at $15,000, Tier 2 at $35,000, Tier 3 at $50,000, Tier 4 at $100,000, Tier 5 at $250,000, and Tier 6 at $500,000.

Tiered rates by category: sports and TCG go 7.75%, 7.5%, 7.25%, 7%, 6.75%, 6.5% from Tier 1 to Tier 6; fashion 7%, 6.5%, 5.5%, 5%, 4.5%, 4.5%; other collectibles 7.25%, 6.5%, 6%, 5%, 5%, 5%; coins 3.9%, 3.8%, 3.7%, 3.6%, 3.55%, 3.5%; everything else 7%, 6.5%, 5.5%, 4%, 4%, 4%.
What commission is charged on: the item sale price (gross merchandise value). Shipping and taxes paid by the buyer are not included.
Payment processing: 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction in the US, calculated on the total order value the buyer pays, including item price, buyer-paid shipping, and taxes.
Cancelled orders are subtracted from your sales total for the period they were placed in, so they do not help you reach a tier.
tips: Watch the $0.30 on cheap lots. A $2 card with $4 shipping pays $0.16 commission but $0.47 processing, about a quarter of the item price. Bundle low-value cards into bigger lots.
Coins are the cheapest category to sell at 4% standard. Do not tag coin lots as 'other collectibles' and pay 8%.
If you are close to $15,000 in a 28-day window, a strong final show can lift the whole next four weeks to Tier 1: 7.75% instead of 8% on sports and TCG, or 7% on fashion.
Buyer-paid shipping is not fee-free. It escapes commission but still pays 2.9% processing, so on a $6 label the fee is about $0.17.
Price for the combined bite: at the standard tier, roughly 10.9% of the item price plus $0.30 and 2.9% of shipping leaves your account on every sports-card sale.

faq.q: What are Whatnot's seller fees in 2026?
faq.a: An 8% commission on the item sale price for most categories (4% for coins), reduced in tiers once your 28-day sales exceed $15,000, plus 2.9% + $0.30 payment processing on the total order value.

faq.q: Does Whatnot charge commission on shipping?
faq.a: No. Commission is calculated on the item price only. The 2.9% + $0.30 processing fee, however, is charged on the full order total including buyer-paid shipping and taxes.

faq.q: How much does Whatnot take on a $100 sale?
faq.a: At the standard tier with $8 buyer-paid shipping: $8.00 commission plus 2.9% of $108 + $0.30 = $3.43 processing, so $11.43 in fees and a payout of $96.57 before your label cost.

faq.q: How do Whatnot's volume tiers work?
faq.a: Your total completed sales across every category and format over a 28-day period set your commission tier for the next 28-day period. Under $15,000 is the standard rate; Tier 1 starts at $15,000 and Tier 6 at $500,000. The rate is locked for the full period.
Yes. A new tiered commission structure took effect September 21, 2026 for existing sellers. Sellers who joined after that date start on the new structure the following Monday.

faq.q: Does Whatnot charge a fee on canceled orders?
faq.a: Cancelled orders are subtracted from your sales total for the period. Refund and cancellation fee handling is covered in Whatnot's help center; it is not modeled here.

faq.q: Is there a listing or monthly fee on Whatnot?
faq.a: No. Whatnot's published schedule is commission plus payment processing; there is no listing fee or subscription.

content.notes: The commission table and processing fee are from Whatnot's US fee schedule as updated for the September 21, 2026 tier structure. Processing is charged on taxes the buyer pays; this calculator does not include tax, so the processing line is slightly low on taxable orders (add 2.9% of the tax). Whatnot runs periodic reduced-commission promotions (for example on electronics, coins, or high-value orders) that are not modeled. Shipping-label pricing, giveaway shipping, and payout timing were not verified on the fee schedule page. Whether a tiered rate is also applied to sellers with the seller-level promotions active is not stated.
